items.root_cause: Every weekly-ad supplement row is one product by construction. The Baker's transcription (grocery-browser-stores-refresh, vision-read flyer pages) writes ONE item and ONE size per flyer line, and compare-deals Add-Norm (:2055 for the bakers/fareway/sams supplement files, :2239-2249 for ads-*.json) normalises whatever it is handed as one name with one size. A Kroger flyer line that sells two different products at one price therefore routes by whichever product's words first-match-wins over commodities.json and divides by whichever size the transcriber wrote, so the basis is right only when both belong to the same product. The engine's only either/or awareness, Test-NameOffersTwoSizes, is consulted solely in the per-each pack-count branches of Get-UnitPrice, sees 19 of the 45 live lines, and never reaches the plain size division that priced the cereal crown. The 09-09 close blocklisted one line of the 45 and left the other 44 and every future flyer on the same path.

root_fix.what: Split at the ingest seam, before matching sees the name, and refuse what cannot be split. (1) A pure function Split-TwoProductAdLine in pricing-math-lib.ps1 beside Test-NameOffersTwoSizes returns one part per product ONLY when every ' or '-separated segment (after stripping a trailing ', In the Bakery' / ', Select Varieties') ends in its own size expression: a number, optionally a range, then fl oz|oz|ct|lb|lbs|pk|pack|rolls|mega rolls|double rolls|ml|l|liter|litre|gal|qt|pt|count|ea, optionally followed by ONE packaging noun (bag|bottle(s)|can(s)|jar|box|pkg|package|carton). A segment with no size is a variety alternation and is glued to the following segment ('Simply Fruit Drink or Ade, 52 fl oz' stays one part). Any segment failing the test leaves the whole line unchanged. (2) compare-deals calls it in the supplement loop (:2050-2056) and emits one Add-Norm per part with the part's own name and the part's own size text (the file row's size is used for a part only when it contains that part's size expression; otherwise the size is cut from the part), stamping split_from = the whole line on each normalised row so audit-match-soundness and the identity table can show provenance. (3) Fail-closed complement for lines the rule leaves whole but Test-NameOffersTwoSizes flags (today 10 Hy-Vee lines, 0 holding a cell): Get-UnitPrice's plain size-division path returns null for such a name, so a two-size line is never again priced by an arbitrary one of its sizes.
root_fix.exact_change: pricing-math-lib.ps1: add Split-TwoProductAdLine([string]$name) -> string[] (1 element = unchanged) using the per-segment test '(?i)\d[\d.\-]*\s*-?\s*(?:fl\.?\s*oz|oz|ct|lbs?|pk|pack|mega\s+rolls?|double\s+rolls?|rolls?|ml|liters?|litres?|\bl\b|gal|qt|pt|count|ea)\b\.?(?:\s+(?:bag|bottles?|cans?|jar|box|pkg|package|carton))?\.?$'; in Get-UnitPrice, immediately before the generic size-division fallthrough: if (Test-NameOffersTwoSizes $deal.name) and the deal carries no split_from, return $null. compare-deals.ps1 :2050-2056: foreach part of (Split-TwoProductAdLine $d.item) call Add-Norm with the part as the name and the part's size text, passing $d as the source row, and carry split_from on the normalised row when the line produced more than one part; the ads-*.json loop at :2239-2249 gets the same call (it fires 0 times on today's file by measurement, and routing it through the one function is the point).

items.subject: Triage residual: Sam's gallon jugs on weight-priced commodities still price off a cent-rounded quotient size
evidence: comparison-2026-09-11 (built 14:27:41): bbq-sauce | Sam's Club | 'Sweet Baby Ray's Original Barbecue Sauce, 1 gal.' | $11.98 | size 171.143 oz | basis 'size 171.143 oz' | $0.07/oz | CROWN, type everyday, membership. Runner-up Walmart | 'Kraft Hint of Honey Slow-Simmered Barbecue Sauce Value Size, 40 oz Bottle' | $2.97 | 40 oz | $0.0743/oz (native 0.074).

The row is a CARRY-FORWARD, not a fresh capture: sams-deals-2026-09-10 and 09-11 hold no gallon-named row at all. It appears in 8 captures from 2026-07-17 to 2026-09-01 (ids 13599611407 then 4W2VMU21D4SI), every one $11.98, sams_unit_price '$0.07/oz', size '171.143 oz', qty_basis 'package; qty derived lp/up'. 171.143 = 11.98 / 0.07. The size is Sam's rounded unit price turned back into a quantity; Select-FreshestCaptureRows keeps it because 09-01 is the freshest capture covering bbq-sauce inside the 90-day window (compare-deals -SamsMaxAgeDays default 90).

What Sam's own arithmetic PROVES about the true size: 11.98 / size rounds to $0.07 only for size in (159.73, 184.31] oz. So the jug is NOT 128 fl oz read as oz (that would print $0.09/oz), Sam's is dividing by a weight, and the true per-oz lies in [0.0650, 0.0750). Walmart's 0.0743 sits INSIDE that band: Sam's beats Walmart only if the jug weighs more than 161.35 oz. The crown is undecidable from any artifact in the estate.

Where the true weight is NOT: the capture rows carry linePrice, unitPrice, name and id only; sams-capture-2026-07-23.csv, vet-sheet.csv, verify-sams-2026-07-31.txt and product-urls.json all repeat the quotient; product-urls.json links https://www.samsclub.com/ip/13599611407, which answered this session with the bot wall 'Let us know you're human (no robots allowed)' (one probe, not retried; Sam's needs an existing real-Chrome tab per the store method). No size was invented for this plan.

THE CLASS, measured over the 90-day window (every sams-deals file dated 2026-06-13 or later, 41 distinct names; the first 14-day pass found 9; the weekly lane's '11' was s5's fl-oz count): rows with qty_basis 'derived lp/up' whose NAME states a unit in another family than Sam's priced unit. 6 hold a cell today: ranch-dressing 0.0858 and hot-sauce 0.1209 (already on the 09-10 name-volume path, priced from the name); turkey-lunchmeat | 'Member's Mark Oven Roasted Turkey Breast, Sliced 1 lb. 6 oz.' | 0.41 (not crown; band [0.4050,0.4150], runner-up Aldi 0.2594 outside); pickles | 'Mt. Olive Kosher Dills Fresh Pack Pickles, 1 gal.' | $6.34 | 126.8 oz | 0.05 CROWN (band [0.0450,0.0550], Walmart 0.0745 OUTSIDE: crown safe, cell +/-10%); bbq-sauce 0.07 CROWN (band [0.0650,0.0750], Walmart 0.0743 INSIDE); glass-cleaner | Sam's Club | 'Windex Original Glass Cleaner, 1 spray bottle + 128 fl. oz. Refill' | $11.72 | size 167.429 fl oz | $0.07/foz CROWN (band [0.0650,0.0750], Walmart 0.0713 INSIDE; the 09-10 fl-oz path refuses this name because it states a refill volume plus an unsized bottle, so it stays a quotient).

So the gallon framing was too narrow. The defect is any crown whose margin over the runner-up is thinner than the derived size's rounding error 0.005/unitPrice. Two such crowns are live today (bbq-sauce, glass-cleaner); the other 35 of the 41 rows hold no cell and surface only when a fresher capture stops covering their commodity.

items.root_cause: build-sams-deals.ps1 Build-Row (:231-233) derives every pack size Sam's did not state in its priced unit as linePrice / cent-rounded unitPrice, so the size and therefore the board per-unit carry a relative error of 0.005/unitPrice (7.1% at $0.07, 10% at $0.05). The row records that it is derived ('qty derived lp/up') and carries sams_unit_price, but neither compare-deals nor any guard reads that basis, so the board ranks a quotient as an exact number and awards a crown by a 6% margin whose error bar is 7%. The 09-10 fix substitutes the name's volume on fl-oz commodities when the name states exactly one volume; a weight commodity has no name-based substitute (a gallon's weight depends on density) and a name with two volumes (Windex bottle + refill) is refused back to the quotient, so the class survives on both, and the crown step cannot see either.

root_fix.what: Carry the derivation's error bar from the row to the crown decision, and give a human-read size a keyed home the builder can verify. (1) compare-deals.ps1: when a Sam's row's qty_basis contains 'derived lp/up', compute pu_rounding_pct = 100 * 0.005 / (unit price parsed from sams_unit_price) in Add-Norm from $srcRow (both fields are on every Sam's row already, including the carried 2026-09-01 row, so no capture is rewritten) and emit it on the board cell. (2) the crown step: when the cheapest cell carries pu_rounding_pct and any other store's per_unit lies within [pu*(1-e), pu*(1+e)], stamp the commodity cheapest_within_rounding = true and cheapest_tie_with = [stores]; the price shown stays the store's own printed unit price and the crown is NOT reassigned (the runner-up is not proven cheaper either). (3) audit-unit-basis-outlier.ps1: new WARN class rounding_band_crown listing every such commodity (2 today), WARN and never HARD because the cell is the store's printed number.
